notes.workingTitle: Billions Sit on Unused Gift Cards. Who Keeps the Money?
notes.centralHook: Somewhere in a drawer, there's a gift card with money still on it. If it's never spent, who ends up with that money?
notes.thesis: An unused balance on a non-expiring card stays spendable, but issuers estimate from their own history how much will not be redeemed and book that share as revenue gradually; unclaimed-property laws may send part to government agencies; federal rules block the quickest ways of taking it (verified dossier hbm-073).
notes.audience: US adults who give or hold gift cards; holiday shoppers
primarySources: Starbucks FY2025 10-K
Darden FY2026 10-K
CFPB Regulation E gift-card rule
Bankrate/YouGov 2024 survey
notes.factualRisk: Low (dossier verified; arithmetic checked; attribution rules in place)
notes.visualPlan: Card balance counters, filing excerpts, money-flow of breakage, three-claimant comparison panel
notes.status: Script exists (session-written, gates passed except packaging + one heuristic opening reading); timed for the holiday gift-card season

notes.factualRisk: Medium: the private company's finances are self-reported; keep claims to what each source states
notes.visualPlan: Can-cost breakdown, distribution map, sponsorship timeline, filing excerpts

notes.centralHook: Walk into a dealer and the watch you want isn't available. Walk across the street and it is, for more. Why?

Brand statements on production and authorised dealers

notes.visualPlan: Retail vs secondary price chart (dated), supply funnel, dealer-allocation diagram
